Reference: Gemini 4 Carbon: our next frontier model
Abstract:
Today, we’re announcing the next frontier model: Gemini 4 Carbon, our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities.

Carbon ranks #1 on the recently updated v5.0 of Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59. It shows significant gains across coding and agentic tasks as well as across key capabilities critical for cybersecurity defense, landing a firm lead in SEC-bench Pro (88.2%) for finding vulnerabilities, ExploitGym (54.8%) for exploitation, and CWE-bench (71.0%) for patching. On internal benchmarks, Carbon drives a strong uplift in generating secure code, and in live coding environments with our own teams it shows reduced misalignment and fabrication rates.

We’ve upgraded Claude Fable and Claude Mythos—models that are designed to tackle the most daunting technical challenges.

Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision. During prerelease testing they’ve helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours—among many other applications we’ll discuss below.

Parameters notes: Inherits size from DeepSeek Flash V4.1 - 748B total, 16B active.
Abstract:
Today, we’re launching Particle to make highly optimized intelligence accessible to everyone. The cost of using capable models still limits who can use them, how often, and what they can build. We’re working to lower that cost by training models to solve problems more efficiently, so people can deploy more intelligence to solve more problems.

Particle-1, post-trained on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, sees large improvements in token efficiency using around ~45% fewer tokens on average across a wide variety of tasks. Many improvements in token optimization only improve on reducing costs but, in this case, tasks finish sooner which is good for end-users. We trained the model in reinforcement learning environments developed internally, with the goal of solving tasks with fewer tokens while maintaining accuracy.

This first release focuses on software engineering. We plan to bring Particle to other domains in future releases.

Reference: Introducing Boba, the social intelligence that understands your goals and community.
Abstract:
Today we are unveiling Boba, the social intelligence that understands your goals and your community.

We built Boba because we believe that people change the world together. What sets Boba apart is Ampersand, a model trained to understand and act on complex real-world goals and values, especially goals that involve multiple people.

Early users have sent over a million messages to Boba. They like Boba's natural voice, memory, and personality, and use it for organization, accountability, and personal improvement. It can make reminders and calendar invites, and use email and research on the web. You can text Boba one-on-one or add it to a group chat. Try it at boba.app.

Today, we’re unveiling Canva Craft, our first state-of-the-art image generation model, developed and trained by Canva Research, our in-house AI lab. Built specifically for design, Craft makes Canva the world’s second most advanced AI lab for image generation, as measured by rankings from DesignArena, the largest crowdsourced assessor of AI design.

Available now in Canva and to developers through our public API, Craft generates stunning, high-quality images at 2K resolution in any aspect ratio. With precise control and editable outputs, Craft gives everyone from first-time creators to professional designers more flexibility to bring their imagination to life.
Accessibility notes: Available through API and Canva's "Dream Lab" site.

Abstract: Mirendil exists to help scientists, engineers and small teams take on their most ambitious problems with AI. We build models and tools to speed up our own research, and plan to make those same tools available to anyone working on hard problems in their own field.

Today we’re introducing Mercury 3, the most capable diffusion-based LLM released to date. Across a range of benchmarks, Mercury 3 outperforms GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5, while running 4–8x faster at 1,000+ tokens per second.

Mercury 3 demonstrates that text diffusion scales. It’s more than 40x larger than Mercury 1 and is vastly more intelligent, but just as fast.
